摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Relation DETR+: Exploring Explicit Position Relation Prior for Dense Prediction

期刊：IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence · DOI：10.1109/tpami.2026.3708265 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

This paper presents a general scheme for enhancing the convergence and performance of DETR (DEtection TRansformer).We investigate the slow convergence problem in transformers from a new perspective, suggesting that it arises from the self-attention that introduces no structural bias on the inputs. To address this issue, we explore incorporating position relation prior as attention bias to augment object detection, following the verification of its statistical significance using a proposed quantitative macroscopic correlation (MC) metric. Our approach introduces an encoder to construct position relation embeddings for progressive attention refinement, which further extends the traditional streaming pipeline of DETR into a contrastive relation pipeline to address the conflicts between non-duplicate predictions and positive supervision. During the progressive refinement process, pattern collapse in multi-layer relations is investigated and alleviated through explicit layer-wise encoding and gated relation modulation. The proposed approach, termed Relation-DETR+, establishes a streamlined relation-enhanced pipeline for dense prediction, capable of jointly addressing object detection, semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and panoptic segmentation tasks within a single framework. Extensive experiments on both generic and task-specific datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. Under the same training schedules, our approach demonstrates superior learning efficiency compared to DINO in detection and Mask-DINO in segmentation, respectively. Moreover, the proposed relation encoder serves as a universal plug-and-play component, bringing clear improvements for theoretically any DETR-like methods. Furthermore, we introduce a large-scale class-agnostic detection dataset, SA-Det-100 k. The experimental results on the dataset illustrate the potential of proposed explicit position relation towards universal object detection.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

LaVIDE: Language-Prompted Satellite Change Detection via Map-Image Alignment

期刊：IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence · DOI：10.1109/tpami.2026.3700146 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Remote sensing change detection based on a map reference and an up-to-date image boosts timely observation of the Earth’s surface when earlier images are lacking for comparison. However, the semantic gap between high-level map categories and low-level image details hinders the extraction of homogeneous features for robust temporal association in change detection. Unlike conventional approaches that either compare pixel-level visual similarity or propagate segmentation errors, we propose a novel framework, Language-VIsion Discriminator for dEtecting changes, LaVIDE, which bridges the semantic gap between high-level map categories and low-level image details using language as an intermediary. Specifically, we introduce restricted prompt learning to generate context-aware textual prompts that align map semantics with image content, and an object-aware embedding enhancement strategy to integrate object-level attributes (e.g., shape, boundary) into map representations. These components enable robust cross-modal alignment within a unified language-vision feature space. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks, DynamicEarthNet, HRSCD, BANDON, and SECOND, demonstrate that LaVIDE outperforms state-of-the-art methods by significant margins, achieving 18.4% and 5.2% improvements in IoU on multi-class and single-class change detection tasks, respectively. Our framework not only advances the accuracy of map-image change detection but also provides a practical solution for rapid map updating with minimal human intervention, promising broad impacts in urban planning, disaster assessment, and ecological conservation.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

No One-Size-Fits-All Neurons: Task-Based Neurons for Artificial Neural Networks

期刊：IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence · DOI：10.1109/tpami.2026.3704202 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

In the past decade, many successful networks are on novel architectures, which almost exclusively use the same type of neurons. Recently, more and more deep learning studies have been inspired by the idea of NeuroAI and the neuronal diversity observed in human brains, leading to the proposal of novel artificial neuron designs. Designing well-performing neurons represents a new dimension relative to designing well-performing neural architectures. Biologically, the brain does not rely on a single type of neuron that universally functions in all aspects. Instead, in our brain, neurons are often task-based. In this study, we address the following question: since the human brain is a task-based neuron user, can the artificial network design go from the task-based architecture design to the task-based neuron design? Since methodologically there are no one-size-fits-all neurons, given the same structure, task-based neurons can enhance the feature representation ability relative to the existing universal neurons due to the intrinsic inductive bias for the task. Specifically, we propose a two-step framework for prototyping task-based neurons. First, symbolic regression is used to identify optimal formulas that fit input data by utilizing base functions such as polynomials. We introduce vectorized symbolic regression (VSR) that stacks all variables in a vector and regularizes each input variable to perform the same computation, which can increase the regression speed, facilitate efficacy in high dimensions, and enable parallel computation. Second, we parameterize the acquired elementary formula to make parameters learnable, which serves as the aggregation function of the neuron. The activation functions such as ReLU and the sigmoidal functions remain the same because they have proven to be good. As the initial step, we evaluate the proposed framework using polynomials as base functions. Empirically, systematic experimental results on synthetic data, classic benchmarks, and real-world applications show that the proposed task-based neuron design is not only feasible but also delivers competitive performance over other state-of-the-art models.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Adaptive Variational Inference: Beyond Bethe, Tree-Reweighted, and Convex Free Energies

期刊：IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence · DOI：10.1109/tpami.2026.3704719 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Variational inference in probabilistic graphical models aims to approximate fundamental quantities such as marginal distributions and the partition function. Popular approaches are the Bethe approximation, tree-reweighted, and other types of convex free energies. These approximations are efficient but can fail when the model is complex and highly interactive. In this work, we analyze two classes of approximations that generalize the above methods as special cases: one resulting from changing the state energy of the model, and the other from choosing a different entropy approximation. We discuss benefits and limitations of each approximation, identify favorable regimes for their parameters, and propose ADAPT-Z_$c$_Z and ADAPT-Z_$\zeta$_Z to automatically detect these optimal settings for a given pairwise binary graphical model. In experiments, we demonstrate their effectiveness for approximating marginals and the partition function.

Wenyang Yang; Hao Zhuang Li; Steven Kwok Keung Chow

官方论文页面link.springer.com · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 论文身份与出版状态证据 DOIdoi.org · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 规范化论文身份

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Deep learning for ECG-based cardiovascular diagnosis: a review of model architectures

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01287-z · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Deep learning has rapidly advanced automated electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation by enabling end-to-end learning of diagnostic patterns from raw or minimally processed signals. Nonetheless, progress remains challenging to compare across studies due to heterogeneous datasets, preprocessing pipelines, and evaluation protocols, with details on external validation and reproducibility often underreported. This review systematically surveys ECG deep learning research published between 2016 and 2025 across major biomedical and engineering databases, complements it with reference screening, and synthesises evidence across various model architectures, input representations, diagnostic tasks, and evaluation practices. The literature is organised into three predominant modelling paradigms: 1D time-series models, 2D transformed representations, and multimodal fusion frameworks. The influence of design choices, such as lead configuration, window length, augmentation, and training objectives, on performance and deployability is summarised. In applications including arrhythmia detection, atrial fibrillation screening, myocardial infarction identification, and multi-label ECG diagnosis, it is observed that reported performance metrics are heavily affected by protocol choices, particularly patient-wise versus segment-wise splitting and the utilisation of external test sets, which constrains the interpretability of primary metrics. Furthermore, emerging directions are highlighted, including efficiency-aware modeling for edge and wearable settings, reliability-aware learning, and privacy-preserving training. Finally, recurring limitations are identified, along with a reproducibility-oriented checklist and reporting recommendations to foster more reliable benchmarking and translation. Overall, while deep learning demonstrates considerable potential.

Tahir Abbas; Zill e Shams; Mohammed M. Alshamiri

官方论文页面link.springer.com · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 论文身份与出版状态证据 DOIdoi.org · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 规范化论文身份

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

A novel q-fractional fuzzy Bonferroni mean based MAGDM model with entropy–TOPSIS and its application to smart education

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01276-2 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

The recent advances in the Internet of Things (IoT) have led to smart education giving rise to the design of smart learning environments. In this environment, the selection of the best IoT-based technology is a complex uncertain multi-criteria decision-making problem. Here, we consider nine IoT-based technologies for education with respect to five criteria to select the best for smart education. To handle the vagueness of the experts’ judgement, we first investigate the q-Rung Orthopair Fuzzy Sets, but they are shown to be invalid if they don’t satisfy some special conditions. Next, we introduce q-fractional fuzzy set to have a more flexible structure for uncertain and inconsistent information. In this context, we propose several family of aggregation operators obtained by using the q-Fractional Fuzzy Sets to account for the proximity between the criteria. Further, a hybrid Entropy-based criteria weight determination and TOPSIS approach is proposed for computing the objective weights of the criteria and ranking the alternatives. The suggested structure will generate a powerful and flexible decision support tool for the education stakeholders that will help them to choose the IoT technologies and play a role in the effective development of a smart learning environment in the presence of uncertainty in decision making. A case study in smart education is presented to illustrate the proposed approach and the findings indicate that Smart Classrooms (T1) are the most suitable IoT-based technology for smart education. Comparative and sensitivity analysis shows the stability, robustness and effectiveness of the proposed method to handle uncertainty and multi-criteria decision making in smart education environments.Keywords: q-Fractional Fuzzy Sets; Internet of Things (IoT); Smart Education; Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM); Entropy-TOPSIS; Aggregation Operators.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Leveraging fruit fly behavior and adaptive velocity for high-performance swarm robotics: the adaptive velocity inspired robot fruit fly algorithm

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01285-1 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

This paper proposes the Adaptive Velocity Inspired Robot Fruit fly Algorithm (AVIRFA), a new approach to swarm intelligence for effectively searching for and tracking multiple targets using multiple robots. Essentially, the AVIRFA algorithm can allow a homogeneous robot team to search for and track stationary and dynamic targets in complex environments, inspired by how fruit flies search for food and implementing an adaptive method from particle swarm optimization. The AVIRFA algorithm continually updates each robot’s velocity and position using both individual and global fitness information, facilitating a balanced exploration-exploitation strategy that enhances search efficiency and reduces the tendency to become trapped in local optima. Simulations were conducted using environments of various size and obstacles, with different target behaviors, providing a comparison of AVIRFA to other recognised algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Fruit fly optimization Algorithm (FOA), Bee Swarm Optimization (BSO), Firefly Algorithm (FA), and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO). As illustrated in the results, AVIRFA reduced average search time by ∼11%, and up to ∼18% when robots started from different regions. Across team sizes of 5 to 20 robots, it maintained the lowest search times with low variability, demonstrating robust, scalable, and cooperative search efficiency across diverse scenarios.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Mountain gazelle optimizer-enhanced hierarchical capsule graph learning networks for industrial robot fault diagnosis

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01288-y · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Robots in industrial processes play an integral role in modern manufacturing; nonetheless, their complex, well-integrated system structures make them prone to failures that may endanger worker safety, reduce performance, and increase production costs. Most conventional fault diagnosis techniques, such as model- and signal-based approaches, often struggle to perform effectively due to interference from high-dimensional, noisy data. Although current machine learning and deep learning approaches have been effective in diagnosing problems, they often depend on hyperparameters, input data, and convergence efficiency. In this research paper, we present a novel framework, HCGLN-MGO, combining the Hierarchical Capsule Graph Learning Network (HCGLN) with the Mountain Gazelle Optimizer (MGO). The sensor and vision fusion data are acquired from the PHME 2021 dataset and harmonized using the Adaptive Sparse Box-Cox Data Harmonization Framework (ASBDHF). The MGO is employed to optimize HCGLN and ensure an appropriate balance between exploration and exploitation of the input data, thereby enhancing fault classification performance. Experimental findings reveal that the formulated method outperforms other existing approaches in accuracy, recall, and F1-score

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

MEPTRIME: an adaptive multi-elite RIME optimizer with piecewise chaotic initialization and smooth tail gating for constrained engineering optimization

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01271-7 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Engineering design optimization frequently involves nonlinear, constrained, and multimodal search spaces where objective/constraint evaluations can be black-box, noisy, or computationally expensive. Under such conditions, population-based metaheuristics remain attractive but often suffer from premature convergence due to over-reliance on a single global leader and from late-stage stagnation caused by overly aggressive parameter decay. To address these issues, this paper proposes MEPTRIME (Multi-Elite Piecewise-chaotic Tail-gated RIME), an enhanced RIME-family optimizer tailored for robust performance on modern benchmarks and engineering design applications. MEPTRIME integrates: (i) piecewise chaotic-map initialization to increase population diversity and improve early exploration; (ii) an adaptive multi-elite guidance mechanism that transitions smoothly from a top- K leader set to a single elite, mitigating early leader bias while strengthening exploitation in later iterations; and (iii) a smooth tail gating strategy for the RimeFactor to prevent abrupt “switch-off” behavior and maintain fine-grained refinements near the end of the search—critical for satisfying tight constraints. Comprehensive experiments on IEEE CEC 2017 (across multiple dimensions) and IEEE CEC 2022, together with representative constrained engineering design problems (e.g., corrugated bulkhead, reinforced concrete beam, and car side impact design), demonstrate that MEPTRIME delivers competitive and frequently superior solution quality and robustness compared with baseline RIME and established metaheuristics, supported by nonparametric statistical testing. These results indicate that the proposed unified enhancements provide a reliable exploration–exploitation transition and improved practicality for real-world engineering design optimization.

官方论文页面link.springer.com · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 论文身份与出版状态证据 DOIdoi.org · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 规范化论文身份

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

ASTER: Adaptive stagnation triggered elite reinitialization operator for population-based metaheuristic algorithms

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01280-6 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Population-based metaheuristic algorithms are widely used to solve optimization problems across different fields. All variants share the same weakness, a collapse of search diversity as the run progresses. The population stagnates before reaching the global optimum. The exploration parameters decay and leave the algorithm unable to recover. Existing remedies, including random restart, increased mutation, and adaptive parameter control, are either destructive of accumulated search knowledge or tightly coupled to a single EA family. This paper proposes and evaluates Adaptive Stagnation Triggered Elite Reinitialization (ASTER), a plug-in algorithm-agnostic operator that wraps around the generational loop of any crossover-based or attraction-based metaheuristic algorithm without modifying its core structure. ASTER integrates four components: stagnation detection, a diversity-gated elite archive that prevents duplicate accumulation, partial population reinitialization with exact size preservation, and exploration parameter reset upon each stagnation event. To demonstrate its effectiveness, ASTER is applied to three fundamentally different population-based frameworks, producing ASTER-GA, ASTER-DE, and ASTER-FA. All variants are evaluated alongside their unenhanced baselines on the CEC 2017 (29 functions, D ∈ {10, 30, 50, 100}), the CEC 2022 benchmark suite (12 functions, D ∈ {10, 20}), and three real-world engineering optimization problems (welded beam, pressure vessel, tension/compression spring). Two established adaptive comparators, jDE and L-SHADE, are additionally included in the CEC suites. Each configuration uses 30 independent runs, with a budget of 10,000 × D fitness evaluations on the CEC suites and 30,000 fitness evaluations on the engineering problems. Statistical analysis uses the nonparametric Wilcoxon signed-rank, the Friedman ranking, and Cohen’s d. ASTER-GA wins on all 29 CEC 2017 functions against Std GA at every tested dimension (D ∈ {10, 30, 50, 100}), with per-function error reductions reaching twelve orders of magnitude; the same pattern holds on CEC 2022 (12/0/0 at both dimensions). ASTER-FA wins on 23 to 28 of 29 CEC 2017 functions against Std FA, replicated on CEC 2022. On three classical constrained engineering design problems, ASTER-GA reduces the mean error gap by roughly two orders of magnitude and rescues Std GA from 53 to 100% feasibility on the spring problem. ASTER-DE operates near neutrally against an already self-adaptive DE baseline. The contribution is therefore scoped as a retrofit that supplies triggered stagnation recovery to hosts lacking parameter adaptation and works as a low-cost safeguard on hosts that already adapt their own parameters.

官方论文页面link.springer.com · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 论文身份与出版状态证据 DOIdoi.org · 2026-11-24 12:16 CST · 规范化论文身份

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

An adaptive elite-guided multi-objective Tiki-Taka algorithm for resource-constrained project scheduling with worker assignment

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01286-0 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

The classical resource-constrained project scheduling problem focuses on minimizing the makespan while assuming all human resources are identical. However, in the context of Industry 5.0, it has become important to consider worker skills, preferences, and well-being as key objectives. This paper introduces a multi-objective, resource-constrained scheduling problem that incorporates worker assignment. The model seeks to minimize makespan, skill-mismatch penalty, and preference-dissatisfaction penalty simultaneously. To achieve this goal, we propose the Adaptive Elite-Guided Multi-Objective Tiki-Taka Algorithm (AEG-MOTTA). This algorithm builds on the original Multi-Objective Tiki-Taka Algorithm but adds adaptive elite guidance, improved selection techniques, and knowledge of skill compatibility and worker preferences. We tested the algorithm on sixteen benchmark problems from PSPLIB and on a real-world case involving gas-turbine maintenance. The results indicate that AEG-MOTTA performs significantly better than six other multi-objective algorithms on key convergence criteria, a superiority rigorously validated by non-parametric statistical testing. While the algorithm exhibits a trade-off in solution diversity, it remains highly competitive and demonstrates superior computational efficiency on large-scale instances. In the industrial case, three evaluation methods converged on the same preferred solution. This solution completed the project before the deadline and achieved a good balance among all three objectives. These findings demonstrate that our model and algorithm can effectively support human-oriented project scheduling in actual industrial environments.

MSSO: a multi-strategy surrogate-assisted optimisation for data clustering

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01283-3 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

The irregular topology and high dimensionality of the search landscape frequently hinder data clustering in high-dimensional spaces. Although metaheuristic algorithms have significant potential, most use inflexible update strategies that cannot adapt to the specifics of the dataset, leading to ineffective refinement. The paper proposes a framework called Multi-Strategy Surrogate Optimisation (MSSO), in which the evolving population is treated as a dynamic surrogate of the objective space. MSSO is a derivative-free mechanism that dynamically adjusts the search radius based on local landscape regularity to stabilise convergence. MSSO combines data-driven exploration, hybrid attraction, and surrogate-guided refinement in a multi-phase optimisation scheme. MSSO achieves directed search by inferring local descent trajectories directly from population spatial interactions via local linear surrogates, combined with a derivative-free adaptive search radius mechanism. Evaluation against nine state-of-the-art metaheuristics, i.e., Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Whale Optimisation Algorithm (WOA), Differential Evolution (DE), Opposition Based Harris-Hawks Optimisation (OHHO), Harris-Hawks Optimisation (HHO), Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA), Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and Butterfly Optimisation Algorithm (BOA) across 11 datasets demonstrates that MSSO achieves a superior average rank of 1.91. Statistical analysis confirms that MSSO achieves statistically significant improvement over six of nine compared baselines while maintaining competitive performance with the top three methods.

论文题名

A topology-aware dual-mode adaptive hybrid genetic algorithm for symmetric and asymmetric traveling salesman problems

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01275-3 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

The symmetric and asymmetric traveling salesman problems require different local-search moves. Segment reversal is valid for symmetric costs, but in ATSP it changes the direction and cost of every internal arc. This paper presents a topology-aware dual-mode adaptive hybrid genetic algorithm (DM-AHGA) that estimates matrix asymmetry and selects an STSP or ATSP search track. Both tracks use collaborative pheromone induction (CPI) to reuse edges or arcs from elite tours and a gain-driven triggering mechanism (GDTM) to decide when offspring receive additional local search. The STSP track combines candidate-set 2-opt with pheromone-guided and bad-edge refinement. The ATSP track uses order-preserving relocation during evolution and VND/ILS refinement afterward. Experiments on 23 STSP and 14 ATSP instances from TSPLIB, together with synthetic Euclidean instances, show that DM-AHGA obtains consistently low optimality gaps on STSP and remains competitive with strong ATSP baselines under matched wall-clock budgets. Ablation results show complementary effects of CPI and GDTM and further improvements from terminal ATSP refinement. Overall, the results support selecting evolutionary operators according to distance-matrix symmetry.

论文题名

SPARC: spatial policy-conditioned actor-critic for multi-robot path planning under partial observability

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01282-4 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Multi-robot path planning under partial observability requires each robot to infer useful spatial information from limited local observations while coordinating with teammates. We present Spatial Policy-Conditioned Actor-Critic (SPARC), a centralized-training/decentralized-execution framework that combines an egocentric spatial actor with per-agent conditional twin critics. The actor preserves local-grid topology through convolution, spatial self-attention, recurrent state modeling, and an explicit goal-direction tensor. During training, each critic estimates values for all candidate actions of the focal agent while conditioning on the global state and sampled teammate-action contexts; the update exactly sums over the nine focal actions and samples only the combinatorial teammate action space. Experiments on benchmark scenarios demonstrate that SPARC achieves higher task returns and lower collision rates compared with QMIX, MAPPO, and IPPO. Ablation studies provide descriptive support for the contributions of spatial representation, attention mechanisms, goal information integration, dynamic-obstacle history, and teammate-conditioned value estimation. Overall, SPARC improves cooperative multi-robot path planning performance under partial observability.

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01284-2 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Atom search optimization (ASO) is a newly developed metaheuristic technique inspired by basic molecular dynamics. However, ASO employs a fixed parameter control scheme and a single learning strategy, which results in insufficient local exploitation capability and makes it susceptible to premature convergence when tackling complex multimodal problems. To alleviate these drawbacks, a competitive learning-based ASO with parameter adaptation (CLASO-PA) is proposed in this work. Specifically, in CLASO-PA, a parameter adaptive mechanism is first introduced to dynamically adjust the control parameters according to the evolutionary state of the population, thereby achieving a better balance between exploration and exploitation. Subsequently, a competitive learning strategy driven by historical population information is developed to improve convergence performance while maintaining population diversity. On this basis, a competitive perturbation mechanism is designed to escape from local optima. The effectiveness of CLASO-PA is evaluated on 42 benchmark functions against ASO and 23 well-established metaheuristic algorithms, and further validated on multi-robot path planning problems. Experimental results demonstrate that CLASO-PA significantly outperforms its competitors in terms of solution accuracy, convergence speed, and statistical rankings. The source code of CLASO-PA is publicly available at https://github.com/lqhgxgl/CLASO-PA.

Healthcare service evaluation using disc spherical fuzzy confidence-level and Yager aggregation-based AHP-CRITIC-COPRAS approach

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01267-3 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Robust evaluation of healthcare services is essential for safeguarding the quality of care, expanding access, and allocating resources judiciously. It also aids in identifying strengths and weaknesses within healthcare services, enabling informed decisions to enhance overall patient care. To meet this need, a confidence level-integrated group decision-making framework is developed. The expert evaluations are modelled using disc spherical fuzzy numbers (DSFNs), an advanced extension of fuzzy theory known for its ability to effectively capture multidimensional uncertainty. This study introduces two novel Yager norm-based aggregation operators for DSFNs, which are embedded in the decision-making model. The weights of experts are determined using the Rank Order Centroid (ROC) method, while the subjective and objective criteria weights are determined using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method, respectively. The confidence levels of experts are included in the decision-making to ensure practical relevance. Lastly, the healthcare services are ranked using the Complex Proportional Assessment (COPRAS) method. The results indicate that communication, expertise, and equipment availability are of the highest importance. Among the hospitals evaluated, Hospital B is found to perform the best. The comparative analysis establishes the practicality of the model, while the sensitivity analysis assesses its robustness. The resulting model provides a transparent, versatile decision-support tool that can sharpen managerial insight and strengthen evidence-based policy in healthcare systems.

Entropy-based q-rung orthopair fuzzy MCDM with linguistic assessments for electric vehicle selection

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01278-0 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

With rising environmental concerns and fossil fuel depletion, electric vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a promising alternative for sustainable transportation; however, selecting the most suitable EV remains challenging due to multiple conflicting criteria and uncertainty in expert evaluations. Since criterion weights can significantly influence the final decision, relying solely on subjective weighting may introduce bias due to differences in expert preferences and judgments. Therefore, along with subjective weighting, an objective weighting mechanism is needed to derive the importance of criteria. To address this issue, an entropy measure is used to determine objective criterion weights, while SWARA-based subjective weights and the integrated weights are considered to examine the effect of different weighting perspectives on EV ranking through q-ROFS-COPRAS. The entropy-derived weights are further compared with existing q-ROFS entropy measures and employed in q-ROFS-TOPSIS, q-ROFS-VIKOR, q-ROFS-WASPAS, q-ROFS-ARAS, and q-ROFS-MABAC to examine the consistency of the resulting rankings. The q-ROFS-COPRAS method yields the ranking E₂ E₄ E₆ E₁ E₃ E₅, which is identical to the rankings obtained using q-ROFS-TOPSIS, q-ROFS-MABAC, and q-ROFS-WASPAS, indicating high degree of consistency among these methods. Furthermore, the applicability of the entropy-based framework is demonstrated through an existing EV selection case study, where the obtained results show substantial agreement with those reported in the literature. Sensitivity analysis for q ranging from 2 to 10 yields an unchanged final ranking, indicating the stability of the decision outcome with respect to variations in the q-rung parameter.

This paper presents a machine learning framework for the automatic classification of rodent navigation strategies in the Barnes maze using geometric feature statistics extracted from trajectory data. Five geometric descriptors are computed from each trajectory. Five statistical measures are then calculated for each descriptor, resulting in a 25-feature representation. The stochastic Nesterov accelerated gradient (SNAG) method is widely used in large-scale machine learning. It computes the stochastic gradient at a look-ahead point generated by the momentum history. The performance of SNAG is sensitive to the choice of step size, and a suitable step size can improve its numerical convergence behavior. Therefore, designing an effective step-size strategy is important for stochastic accelerated optimization. This paper focuses on the SNAG framework and proposes an adaptive step-size scheme. Specifically, we introduce a stochastic Nesterov accelerated gradient method with an adaptive Polyak step size, termed SNAG-APS. SNAG-APS evaluates both the stochastic loss and gradient at the Nesterov extrapolation point and uses a momentum-dependent scaling factor in the adaptive step size. The main contributions of this paper include: (i) We design SNAG-APS by combining a Polyak-type adaptive step size with stochastic Nesterov acceleration. (ii) Under standard smoothness assumptions and the weak growth condition, we establish a nonconvex stationarity bound for SNAG-APS, which contains a decreasing term and a residual term. (iii) Experiments on classical machine learning datasets and deep neural network benchmarks show that SNAG-APS achieves competitive numerical performance compared with several optimization algorithms.

In recent years, metaheuristic optimization algorithms have emerged as effective tools for identifying optimal parameter values. This paper presents an effective parameter identification method based on a newly proposed optimizer, namely the Modified Stochastic Paint Optimizer (mSPO). This algorithm is applied to identify the parameters of the Shepherd’s electric vehicle model. In this work, the original Stochastic Paint Optimizer (SPO) is enhanced by incorporating a memory-based elite solution guidance strategy to produce the mSPO. This modification helps to avoid the common pitfalls in high-dimensional optimization landscapes, such as premature convergence, and prevents the algorithm from becoming trapped in local minima. Additionally, the adaptive mutation strategy is employed to dynamically adjust the balance between exploration and exploitation based on the results of previous iterations. These improvements enable the mSPO to provide a faster and more accurate convergence curve, making it a highly effective tool for solving complex optimization problems such as battery parameter identification. The performance of the mSPO is compared with six other competitive algorithms, including the SPO, COOT, ROA, AOA, OOA, and PSO. The comparison encompasses optimizing ten different CEC2022 benchmark functions as well as the Li-ion battery models. Based on the average cost function, the mSPO is ranked first among the other optimizers. Furthermore, the identification method using the modified mSPO proved highly effective in ascertaining the battery’s unidentified characteristics. The lowest average cost function value of 0.01028 was attained by mSPO, followed by ROA at 0.01223, whereas the worst value of 0.07409 was obtained by AOA. Therefore, the outstanding results of the mSPO proved that it is a promising competitor.

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01274-4 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

The rapid growth of e-commerce and retail distribution has increased the need for efficient last-mile delivery systems that jointly account for courier availability, order prioritization, and routing decisions. This study addresses this challenge by integrating courier assignment, order dispatching, and route planning within a unified optimization framework. A mixed-integer linear programming model is developed to represent the problem and provide optimal reference solutions for small-scale instances. Fitness landscape analysis is then used to characterize the underlying search space and identify the need for a search strategy that combines diversification and intensification. Based on these insights, a hybrid adaptive large neighborhood search–genetic algorithm is developed, while the standalone adaptive large neighborhood search and genetic algorithm are implemented as comparative approaches. Computational results show that all three methods provide high-quality solutions for small instances, while the hybrid approach consistently achieves better solution quality and robustness with competitive computational efficiency as problem complexity increases. Non-parametric statistical tests further support the observed performance differences. These findings are consistent with the search-design implications derived from the fitness landscape analysis, highlighting the benefit of combining population-based diversification with adaptive neighborhood-based intensification for complex last-mile delivery problems. Beyond algorithmic performance, the study compares open- and closed-loop routing strategies and shows that their relative advantages depend on operational conditions and order distribution. The results provide practical guidance for designing efficient last-mile delivery systems while demonstrating how landscape-informed hybrid optimization can support solution-method design for complex routing problems.

Symbolic Regression (SR) problems are extensively solved using Gene Expression Programming (GEP); however, traditional GEP often suffers from premature convergence and a high proportion of invalid gene expressions. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel algorithm aiming to significantly improve convergence speed and model learning efficiency. The proposed methodology introduces an altered chromosome structure by adding a gene weight domain. This domain is dynamically optimized using the Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) algorithm, which evaluates and refines weights via a two-stage teacher-student mechanism. The algorithm was evaluated against 16 varied standard SR cases and a practical H62 brass corner milling application. Experimental results demonstrate that TLBO-GEP eliminates inferior genes and drastically accelerates convergence. Specifically, in the engineering case, TLBO-GEP achieved an exceptionally low average prediction relative error of 2.59%, significantly outperforming standard GEP (9.27%), BPNN (11.80%), and SVM (6.01%). In conclusion, while facing minor limitations with deeply nested exponential functions, the integration of TLBO into GEP provides a highly robust, efficient, and precise mathematical modeling tool for complex predictive applications.

A novel hybrid and quantum-augmented variant of particle swarm optimization algorithm to solve large-scale and non-convex economic emission dispatch problems in power systems

This paper presents a novel hybrid optimization algorithm to solve large-scale and non-convex Economic Emission Dispatch (EED) problems in power systems. The proposed algorithm incorporates quantum-inspired operators into the velocity update mechanism of standard Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, aiming to enhance population diversity and convergence efficiency in high-dimensional search spaces. In addition, the proposed algorithm is enhanced via a fuzzy interface system to dynamically adopt the inertia weight of the particles in the course of iterations. Finally, it is hybridized with Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) to significantly improve the exploration and exploitation processes in the search space of the problem. Hence, this paper introduces a Hybrid Quantum-Augmented PSO-GWO (HQAPSO-GWO) algorithm to tackle one of the most important problems in power system operation. To model the realistic and complex characteristics of power generation, the cost function integrates Valve-Point Loading Effects (VPLEs), introducing non-convexity and multiple local minima into the problem landscape. The effectiveness of the proposed HQAPSO-GWO is evaluated on several unimodal and multi-modal benchmark optimization problems as well as different EED scenarios over a challenging 40-unit test system, demonstrating superior solution quality and computational performance compared to existing state-of-the-art algorithms. Simulation results confirm that the HQAPSO-GWO algorithm provides a robust and scalable solution methodology for modern EED problems, making it a promising approach for large-scale power system optimization. For instance, the proposed algorithm achieved a reduction of 2.4% in the total generation cost for the 40-unit system compared to existing algorithms, translating to an annual savings of over $25 M. Furthermore, it identified the optimal solution in almost 100% less computational time, highlighting its suitability for real-time applications by power system operators in daily operational planning.

In recent years, micro multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (μMOEAs) have achieved promising performance in solving practical problems on low-power microprocessors. However, effectively balancing multiple conflicting objectives under the limited computational resources of low-power microprocessors remains challenging. Therefore, this paper proposes a micro multi-operator multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm with a Chebyshev spacing indicator (μMMPSO-CS). The algorithm alternately employs three particle swarm operators with complementary search characteristics to improve the convergence and diversity of the micro-population. Meanwhile, an adaptive weight-vector update triggering mechanism based on the Chebyshev spacing indicator is designed. The weight vectors are updated only when a significant loss of diversity is detected, thereby reducing unnecessary computational operations. The proposed μMMPSO-CS is compared with six multi-objective optimization algorithms on 21 test problems from the WFG, ZDT, and DTLZ benchmark suites. The experimental results show that μMMPSO-CS achieves the best IGD results on 12 problems and the best HV results on 14 problems, demonstrating strong overall performance. Finally, simulations on two real-world problems, MLDMP and MPDMP, based on low-power microprocessors confirm that the proposed algorithm is suitable for resource-constrained multi-objective optimization applications.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

A fusional WWOA-CCSA-TPSO algorithm with the three control mechanisms for long-term rumor refutation in online social networks

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01289-x · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Currently, social media platforms have accelerated information dissemination in Online Social Networks (OSNs) while also enabling the rapid and persistent spread of rumors. Owing to their fast diffusion, complex evolution, and the difficulty of long-term governance, rumor refutation remains challenging. Existing methods still have limited capacity to jointly model authoritative intervention, audience retransmission disturbance, and dynamic cognitive evolution within a unified framework. To address this problem, this paper proposes a fusional Wave Whale Optimization Algorithm-based Chaotic Crow Search Algorithm and Time-varying Particle Swarm Optimization (FWWOA-CCSA-TPSO) algorithm for long-term rumor refutation under three control mechanisms. The FWWOA-CCSA-TPSO framework integrates three tailored meta-heuristics into a cohesive control loop: the Wave Whale Optimization Algorithm (WWOA) serves as the primary driver for authoritative truth injection by optimizing audience reach under resource constraints; the information then flows into a retransmission-distortion layer modeled by the Chaotic Crow Search Algorithm (CCSA), which captures stochastic semantic drift during peer-to-peer interactions; and the Time-varying Particle Swarm Optimization (TPSO) controls the dynamic cognitive convergence of the population, using time-varying learning factors to guide the transition from individual skepticism to collective truth belief. By formulating long-term rumor refutation as a truth-belief maximization task, we evaluate the framework through ablation and comparative simulations. The results demonstrate that the synergetic integration of the three control mechanisms significantly enhances convergence and refutation effectiveness over the selected meta-heuristic baselines under the current simulation setting. The results validate the proposed framework as a robust and simulation-oriented approach for long-term rumor governance in OSNs.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Chaotic and hyperchaotic weight initialization with dual-branch temporal learning in informer for long-term time-series forecasting

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01291-3 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Long-term time-series forecasting supports decision-making in energy management, industrial monitoring, and predictive maintenance. Capturing nonlinear patterns and temporal dependencies across multiple scales remains challenging, while neural network weight initialization can influence optimization and predictive accuracy. This study investigates chaotic and hyperchaotic weight initialization within a hybrid TCN-Informer architecture. Initialization sequences are generated from corresponding dynamical systems and processed through transient removal, normalization, and layer-dependent scaling before assignment to selected weights. The architecture combines dilated causal convolutions with attention-based temporal learning through adaptive gated fusion to capture temporal dependencies at multiple scales. Extensive experiments on four ETT benchmark datasets across five prediction horizons and five matched random seeds under a consistent experimental protocol show that the strongest improvements occur on ETTh1 and ETTm1. Compared with Standard Informer, hyperchaotically initialized TCN-Informer reduces mean squared error (MSE) by 17.6–26.0% on ETTh1 and 26.6–31.8% on ETTm1 across two prediction horizons. Relative to standard TCN-Informer, chaotic and hyperchaotic initialization achieve maximum MSE reductions of 31.6% on ETTm1 and 31.7% on ETTh1, respectively. Additional analyses examine the influence of initialization on weight characteristics, convergence, and gradient dynamics, alongside the contribution of hybrid temporal learning. The findings highlight the potential of dynamically generated initialization and complementary temporal representations for improved long-term forecasting, with benefits dependent on the dataset and prediction horizon.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

DFBTO: search-feedback-driven dynamic feature-space adaptation for high-dimensional text feature selection

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01293-1 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

High-dimensional text feature selection remains challenging because wrapper-based optimization must explore an exponentially large subset space while repeatedly evaluating candidate subsets using a classifier. Although filter methods can provide useful relevance information, fixed filtering may prematurely restrict the search and prevent later reconsideration of informative features. To address this limitation, this study proposes DFBTO, a search-feedback-driven dynamic feature-space adaptation framework built on the Barrel Theory-Based Optimizer (BTO). DFBTO uses ReliefF only as an initial relevance prior and progressively shifts feature priority toward retained wrapper-search evidence obtained from elite and current-best solutions. The active feature domain is gradually contracted, while all original features remain eligible for repeated full-domain reranking and possible re-entry. A bounded elite-directed refinement is further introduced, and all reconstruction evaluations are charged to the same function-evaluation budget. Experiments on 15 high-dimensional text datasets show that DFBTO achieved the best average OptimizerFitness rank and obtained lower dataset-level mean OptimizerFitness than every search-based comparator on all datasets. DFBTO retained 31.8% of the original features on average, corresponding to a 68.2% reduction, and selected fewer features than its parent BTO on every dataset. The paired tests did not detect a statistically significant difference in held-out Macro-F1 relative to BTO or the full-feature Linear SVM. DFBTO was also faster than BTO on 14 of the 15 datasets. Ablation, mechanism, and sensitivity analyses further support the role of dynamic feature-space adaptation in the observed search and compactness outcomes.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Complex pythagorean parameterized fuzzy models for multi-attribute group decision-making for smart city project selection

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01294-0 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

The development of smart cities in a sustainable way presupposes the systematic assessment of any complex infrastructural project in the context of uncertainty, balancing technological, economic, environmental, social and benefits, governance needs, and innovation opportunities. The focus of this research is the essential issue of choosing the most important smart city projects among 15 options. To address expert hesitation and periodic fluctuations, we propose the complex Pythagorean parameterized fuzzy Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution model. The applicability of the framework is illustrated through a synthetic numerical case study with simulated evaluations from 15 hypothetical domain experts, 15 alternatives, and 30 criteria. The outcomes show that smart water resource management (D₃) is the highest-ranked alternative, and sensitivity analysis across weight variations confirmed the stability of the ranking. A comparative study with established methods has shown that some methods have strong correlations with the proposed method. The proposed model provides a transparent and auditable decision-support model for urban planning.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Escaping stagnation in penalty-based constrained particle swarm optimization with bounded-potential quantum-inspired displacement

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01292-2 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

This paper investigates the role of bounded-potential quantum-inspired displacement in penalty-based constrained particle swarm optimization. Starting from an improved particle swarm optimizer (IPSO) with a quadratic penalty, the velocity update is replaced by displacement laws derived from the Lorentz, Rosen–Morse and Coulomb-like square-root potential fields, giving three quantum-inspired variants (QI-PSO). A log-contraction condition is derived that characterises the almost-sure convergence of a stagnated particle for an arbitrary displacement kernel, together with a bound on the expected number of iterations needed to reach a better basin of attraction. The variants are compared with IPSO, constricted PSO and standard quantum-behaved PSO on two-dimensional constrained benchmarks under several penalty constants, on CEC 2006 constrained problems, on higher-dimensional constrained problems and on a classical unconstrained suite. Penalty, feasibility-rule and ε-constraint handling are considered, and nonparametric statistical tests are used throughout. The results show that quantum-inspired displacement improves reliability: it reduces the number of runs that stagnate in non-global basins, most clearly on the constrained Rastrigin problem, while IPSO retains higher precision on smooth landscapes. On higher-dimensional problems QI-PSO-CS significantly improves on IPSO on 12 of 23 classical functions and on 4 of 6 constrained problems in 10 and 30 dimensions, and on ten CEC 2006 problems with feasibility rules it attains the best overall rank, statistically on a par with standard quantum-behaved PSO. A parameterised-kernel study shows that kernels with a zero log-contraction exponent attain the lowest final accuracy irrespective of their tail index, and a contraction–expansion schedule derived from the theory further improves the precision of QI-PSO.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

An effective hyper-heuristic for the single-depot multiple traveling salesman problems

期刊：Evolutionary Intelligence · DOI：10.1007/s12065-026-01281-5 · 摘要来源：已核验来源

Here, the genetic algorithm is customized for the single depot multiple traveling salesman problems (SDMTSP) using roulette wheel selection, cyclic crossover, and K-opt for mutation. Similarly, the artificial bee colony is redesigned using the swap operation, and K-Opt and differential evolution are modified using the swap operation, K-Opt for mutation, and cyclic crossover for the SDMTSPs. Finally, three customized heuristics are coordinated to design an efficient hyper-heuristic, termed eH-SDMTSP for the SDMTSPs. It involves two disjoint phases. In the first phase, three customized heuristics are applied independently on three separate populations for some iterations to produce multiple promising solution zones. At the end of this phase, a new population of the same cardinality is created, taking better solutions from three modified populations. The second phase starts with the new population and the heuristic that modified the global best solution last. The search process adaptively switches to the next heuristic when the global best solution becomes stagnant. Experimental results on benchmark instances from TSPLIB demonstrate that eH-SDMTSP outperforms several state-of-the-art algorithms in accuracy, efficiency, and consistency. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method are further validated through extensive statistical analysis.
